R1.description: Pure helpers map a Codex worker result to the job's launch options, the stream-file text and the builder of a derived `usage_record`, importing nothing from `job`, with the existing `job.py` helpers (`_worker_dict`, `_usage_fields`, `_codex_tester_telemetry`) reused where they are (#260)

R2.description: The job layer records a completed Codex worker run through a launcher-keyed branch, in the Claude record's shape: outcome, stream files, `worker_process`, `ownership_tag`, `usage_record`, the unchanged transition verification or, for a protocol decision, the Workflow's own `reconcile`, no usage reservation, the operator's Codex home for the credential copy-back, and a breach that never ends `FINISHED`; the Claude path is unchanged (#260)

R3.description: Every path ends the record or leaves it where `resume` expects: a refusal or a missing tree is a terminal `WorkerNotStarted`, an interrupt leaves `LAUNCHED`, any other fault ends `FAILED`, and the credential copy is gone after each (#260)

R4.description: Nothing real reaches the branch: no real launcher key, Codex worker role, setting, option, exit code or gate; the tree is a seam (default refusal) and H4c2 is named, with the live proof recorded and the guides and roadmap stating it (#260)
